edit.description: The one home. `one_clause_contract` (:1053) already builds an engine `Contract` over one labelled `Clause`, but it fixes `Severity::Required` and passes `None` as `clause_label`'s third argument, where the shipped stamper (`drift::stamp_clause_label`, src/drift.rs:1640) labels off the row's `field` column. Split it into the two jobs its five hand-built twins spell separately: a `Clause` builder taking `(kind, severity, predicate)` and labelling `contract::clause_label(Some(kind), predicate.key(), predicate.target())` with `guidance`/`source` at `None`, and a `Contract` builder taking `(kind, clauses)` — closed_keys' `hook` case binds two clauses to one contract, so the multi-clause form is required, not speculative. `one_clause_contract` then composes the two and keeps its signature, so `one_clause_findings` (:1073) and `one_clause_admissibility` (:1087) are unchanged at their call sites. `predicate.target()` reproduces the emitted `field` column for every predicate these suites name (Required/Optional/Type/Shape/Membership/Unique = the field; ClosedKeys/Extent/Kind/FormatPlacesEdges = `None`).

Two of the six spellings. `clause(severity, predicate)` (:21) is the labeller verbatim at kind `plugin-manifest` and `contract(clauses)` (:32) the contract builder verbatim; both delegate to the home, keeping their per-suite kind binding in one line each — the shape `field_addressing::findings` already has over `common::one_clause_findings`. The `hook_clause` closure (:276) and the `Contract` literal below it (:283) are a third, inline spelling at kind `hook`: they go to the home directly. `declares_name` (:41), `declares` (:51) and `closes` (:61) compose the local `clause` and are unaffected. `use temper::contract::{self, Clause, Contract, ...}` narrows as the literals leave; clippy runs at -D warnings.

`clause(unit, max, whole)` (:32) builds `Predicate::Extent` and then spells the labeller at kind `skill`, severity `Advisory` — the one call site proving the severity parameter is not constant across the family. It keeps its predicate-building job and delegates the `Clause` build; `contract(unit, max, whole)` (:44) delegates the `Contract` build. `selection` (:53) reads the local `clause` and is unaffected.

`shaped(field, shape)` (:34) inlines both jobs at once — `Predicate::Shape` then the labelled `Clause` inside a `Contract` literal at kind `skill`. It keeps building its predicate and delegates the rest. Its three `rule` assertions (:67, :110, :147) pin `skill.shape.name`/`skill.shape.description`, which `predicate.target()` reproduces exactly, so they do not move.

The `bare_contract` closure (:289) is the sixth spelling, at kind `kind-clause-fixture`, and is the one that already passes `None` for the label's third argument — correct there only because `Predicate::Kind` has no target, which the home now derives instead of hard-coding. Its `rule` assertion (:326) pins `kind-clause-fixture.kind` and does not move. `places_edges_contract` (:358) hand-spells the literal `"citation.format-places-edges"` rather than calling the labeller; it folds onto the home, and its assertion (:412) pins the same string `predicate.key()` yields.

The assertion the split was hiding. `:119` pins `wrong[0].rule` at `pack.type`, which only holds because `one_clause_contract` hard-codes `None`; a real lock stamps `pack.type.keywords` (the row's `field` column, src/drift.rs:1646). The assertion moves to the shipped address. The suite's `findings` wrapper (:70) and `one_clause_admissibility` call (:210) are unchanged.

summary: A one-clause engine contract is built six ways across five suites, and the shared home labels with `None` where a real lock stamps the clause's field.

tests.asserts: a one-clause `type` contract over field `keywords` fires a finding whose rule is the address a real lock stamps, `pack.type.keywords`, not the unqualified `pack.type` the hard-coded `None` produced
the four closed-keys properties and the embedded `hook` pairing hold unchanged with every clause and contract built through the one home

acceptance: `cargo test` green with one home building every labelled engine clause and one-clause contract across the five suites, `pack.type.keywords` asserted as the shipped address, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean of the imports the folded literals strand.
notes: Excluded: section_contains.rs:35 and lock_declaration_rows.rs:1105 hand-spell `spec.section_contains`; SectionContains is one of four predicates whose emitted `field` the SDK synthesizes (declarations.ts:189, `heading.marker`), so `predicate.target()` there would author a third spelling of a label the tool never stamps — and the shipped address is already proven at lock_declaration_rows.rs:3586. field_addressing.rs is label-blind (messages only), so no edit. scoped at ff6e6072
